features.title: Random Note

readme.excerpt: This trig param introduces an element of random to your selected notes. A value of 0 will leave the note unchanged. A value of 1 will randomly give your existing note or the note one higher in the scale. A value of 2 will randomly give your existing note, the note one higher in your selected scale, or the note one lower. A value of 3 will randomly select notes -1, 0, 1 or 2. A value of 4 will randomly select notes -2, -1, 0, 1 or 2. And so on. Use trig locks to really spice things up. These can be combined with random twos note trig param. By default, random notes are quantised to the pentatonic version of the currently selected scale to reduce the chance of dissonant harmonic interactions. This can be disabled in _Mosaic_'s param settings. With Lock random to pent. enabled, a nonzero sum of Random Note and Random Twos offsets triggers nearest-pentatonic snapping for ordinary notes and fully quantised note masks, in either direction. Zero sums, including cancellation, do not trigger this option; other applicable pentatonic options still apply. Equal-distance pitches choose the lower note. Snap-only and unquantised masks retain their chromatic random-offset behaviour. Fixed Note and Quantised Fixed Note retain their override precedence.

details.title: How the value sets the range
details.text: Random Note n adds a random scale-degree offset. n = 1 gives 0 or +1, 2 gives -1 to +1, 3 gives -1 to +2 and 4 gives -2 to +2. Random Twos Note uses the same ranges in steps of two degrees. When both are set the offsets add, so 4 and 4 can move a note by up to 6 degrees either way. Each pass draws new offsets; the manual examples use a fixed seed so that they repeat exactly.

features.title: Random Twos Note

readme.excerpt: Similar to random note, this trig param introduces an element of random to your selected notes. The difference here is that twos note restricts values to those divisible by two. A value of 0 will leave the note unchanged. A value of 1 will randomly give your existing note or the note two higher in the scale. A value of 2 will randomly give your existing note, the note two higher in your selected scale, or the note two lower. A value of 3 will randomly select notes -2, 0, 2 or 4. A value of 4 will randomly select notes -4, -2, 0, 2 or 4. And so on. Use trig locks to really spice things up. These can be combined with random note trig params. Again, random notes are quantised to the pentatonic version of the currently selected scale to reduce the chance of dissonant harmonic interactions. This can be disabled in _Mosaic_'s param settings.

readme.excerpt: The Chord Strum param dynamically spaces selected chord masks using the selected step division, ensuring they align rhythmically with the channel's settings. Notes are quantised to the current scale, adjusting in real-time if the scale changes mid-strum, guaranteeing each note stays harmonious and in tune, regardless of strum duration. Each chord note is played once. Empty mask slots keep their positions in the selected chord shape and consume spacing and acceleration ordinals, including trailing empty slots.

details.title: Division values
details.text: Strum values are lengths in channel steps: 1/24 is the shortest and 128 the longest; X switches strumming off. Turning E3 down stops at X and turning it up stops at 128. 1/2 puts half a step between successive chord notes. Each chord note starts at its strum time and then lasts the note length from its own start.

features.title: Chord Arpeggio

readme.excerpt:
The Chord Arp param is similar to Chord Strum, but chord masks are looped at the current step division for the length of the current step. Notes are quantised to the current scale. Empty chord masks are treated as rests, allowing for rhymic patterns. Arpeggios also honour the Chord Velocity and Chord Shape modifiers. The Chord Arpeggio param overrules the chord strum param. Chord arpeggios can also be used as ratchets if no chord masks are set.

With Chord Spread at zero, the first arp interval is one full selected division of the channel step. For example, a half-step arp on a two-step note advances through its slots at 0, 1/2, 1 and 1 1/2 steps; it does not start another note at the two-step endpoint. Each arp note lasts one selected division from its own onset, shortened when necessary to finish at the original note's endpoint.

Starting another arp on the same channel cancels the old arp's future notes. Notes already sounding keep their remaining duration, capped by their original endpoint; the old arp's endpoint does not cut notes from its replacement. Pattern resets likewise preserve the remaining duration of sounding notes. Stop releases sounding notes and cancels future arp notes. Overlapping notes of the same MIDI pitch still send a corresponding Note Off for each Note On; how a receiving instrument handles overlapping voices is unchanged.

Chord Shape orders the root and four chord-mask slots. An empty mask slot, or a muted root slot, is a rest and keeps its position, including at the end of the sequence. Rest slots consume the same time and acceleration ordinal as sounding slots. If no chord masks are populated, an unmuted root instead forms a one-slot ratchet; if the root is also muted, the result is silence.

edge_cases: With Chord Spread at zero, the first arp interval is one full selected division of the channel step. For example, a half-step arp on a two-step note advances through its slots at 0, 1/2, 1 and 1 1/2 steps; it does not start another note at the two-step endpoint. Each arp note lasts one selected division from its own onset, shortened when necessary to finish at the original note's endpoint.

Starting another arp on the same channel cancels the old arp's future notes. Notes already sounding keep their remaining duration, capped by their original endpoint; the old arp's endpoint does not cut notes from its replacement. Pattern resets likewise preserve the remaining duration of sounding notes. Stop releases sounding notes and cancels future arp notes. Overlapping notes of the same MIDI pitch still send a corresponding Note Off for each Note On; how a receiving instrument handles overlapping voices is unchanged.

features.title: Chord Acceleration

readme.excerpt:
Chord Acceleration modifies the spacing of an enabled Strum or Arpeggio together with Chord Spread. Off (0) means no progressive change: every gap is the selected division plus Spread. A positive value lengthens each following gap; a negative value shortens it. With Spread at zero, Acceleration has no effect.

In channel-step units, let `d` be the Strum or Arp division, `s` be Spread, and `a` be Acceleration (zero when off). The gap before slot `k`, counting the first gap as 1, is `d + s * (1 + (k - 1) * a)`. The first slot occurs at trigger time; later slot times are the sums of these gaps. A new trigger restarts the ordinal. Wrapping an arp's slots does not restart it. These are the nominal musical times before swing and clock-pulse quantisation. An arp interval occupies at least one scheduler pulse, including after swing. At fast channel rates, this limits the resolution of very short gaps.

For a division of 1/2 and Spread of 1/4:

| Acceleration | Successive gaps | Slot times from the trigger |
|---|---|---|
| Off | 3/4, 3/4, 3/4, 3/4 | 0, 3/4, 3/2, 9/4, 3 |
| +1 | 3/4, 1, 5/4, 3/2 | 0, 3/4, 7/4, 3, 9/2 |
| +2 | 3/4, 5/4, 7/4, 9/4 | 0, 3/4, 2, 15/4, 6 |
| -1 | 3/4, 1/2, 1/4, then 0 | 0, 3/4, 5/4, 3/2, then stop |

When the next gap is zero or negative, scheduling ends before that slot. There is no extra simultaneous note or reversed time; notes already sounding retain their releases. Empty slots, including trailing rests, advance the same ordinal in both strums and arps.

details.title: Worked example: a strum that stops early
details.text: Fill only Chd1 and Chd4, set Chord Pattern to reverse (<-), Strum to 1/2, Spread to 1/4 and Chord Accel Mod to -1. The order is slot 4, 3, 2, 1, root. Slot 4 sounds at once; slot 3 is empty and follows 3/4 step later; slot 2 is empty and follows 1/2 step after that; slot 1 sounds 1/4 step after that, 1 1/2 steps after the trigger. The gap before the root would be 0, so the root never sounds.

features.title: Chord Spread

readme.excerpt: Chord Spread adds a duration to the selected Strum or Arp division, measured in channel steps. For example, a half-step division with quarter-step Spread starts with a three-quarter-step gap. With Acceleration off, all gaps stay at that value. With Acceleration enabled, each following gap changes by Spread multiplied by Acceleration, as above. Spacing modifiers act only when Strum or Arpeggio is enabled and do not change the selected note length. Arp notes remain limited by their original note endpoint.

readme.excerpt: The Chord Velocity Modifier incrementally adjusts the velocity of successive notes in a chord, starting from the chord's root note. This adjustment can either increase or decrease the velocity, thereby creating a "swell" effect for rising intensity or a "fade" effect for a diminishing feel.

controls.gesture: Hold a sequencer step + E3
controls.result: Set that step’s parameter lock; clear it with held step + K2 to return to the channel default.

details.title: Orders
details.text: -> plays the root then chord slots 1-4. <- reverses the order: it plays slots 4-1 then the root. X applies no shape: the root plays first. With no strum the voices start together, so a shape matters most with Strum or Arpeggio. A step lock set to X returns that step to root-first. -><- alternates between the start and the end of that order, working inward: root, slot 4, slot 1, slot 3, slot 2. <--> does the same starting from the end: slot 4, root, slot 3, slot 1, slot 2.

features.title: Mute Root Note

readme.excerpt: The Mute Root Note param allows you to silence the root note of a chord while allowing other chord notes to play. When enabled, any chord played on that step will omit its root note while still playing all other chord notes. This can be used to create more varied chord voicings and inversions.

controls.gesture: Channel tasks → Trig params → E2 slot → K2 → E3 Mute Chord Root → K3 → K2
controls.result: Assign Mute Chord Root to one of the ten slots.

controls.gesture: E3 with no grid step held
controls.result: Edit the channel default: OFF or ON.

controls.gesture: Hold a sequencer step + E3
controls.result: Set that step’s parameter lock; clear it with held step + K2 to return to the channel default.

feedback: The Mute Root Note param allows you to silence the root note of a chord while allowing other chord notes to play. When enabled, any chord played on that step will omit its root note while still playing all other chord notes. This can be used to create more varied chord voicings and inversions.

requirements.statement: Mute-root omits root while retaining other voices.
oracles: Exact retained voice identities and silence for omitted root, no stuck notes.

features.title: Fully Quantise Mask

readme.excerpt: The Fully Quantise Mask param controls whether note masks on a step are fully quantised to the current scale, including scale degree and rotation adjustments. When enabled, note masks will be quantised to match the current scale's settings exactly. This can be used to override the global quantization settings on a per-channel or per-step basis, allowing for more precise control over how note masks interact with scale changes. Channel X uses the global Quantise note masks setting; explicit Off and On override it. An explicit step X uses the global setting directly, bypassing the channel value. Clearing that step lock instead restores the channel value (and therefore the global setting if the channel is X).

controls.result: Edit the channel default: X, OFF or ON.

controls.gesture: Hold a sequencer step + E3
controls.result: Set that step’s parameter lock; clear it with held step + K2 to return to the channel default.

details.title: How the three levels combine
details.text: The most specific setting wins: an explicit step lock first, then the channel value, then the global Quantise note masks option. X means no choice at that level. A channel X uses the global option. A step X skips the channel value and uses the global option directly. Use On when written masks should follow Degree, Rotation and scale changes; leave it Off or X when masks should stay as written.

features.title: Scale Editor

readme.excerpt:
Access the scale editor by pressing the second global menu button. When in the scale editor, a short press of the scale buttons selects one of the 16 scales; the currently selected scale is brightly lit on the grid. A short press on the already applied scale turns the global scale off while retaining that slot for editing; another short press applies it again. With global scale off and no scale lock, pattern degrees play as chromatic semitone offsets. All patterns now default to this scale unless overridden by a global scale trig lock or channel scale trig lock. Use the Scale screen to adjust the root, scale, degree, rotation and transposition for the selected scale: E2 chooses a setting, E3 changes it, K3 applies it and K2 cancels. The title row names the slot being edited. A shift press (hold K1) selects a scale slot for editing without changing the global scale selection. A long press on a different editing slot does the same. A long press on the slot already selected for editing turns the global scale off and clears the editing selection. Selecting a slot for editing does not switch playback to it; however, saving changes to a scale already used by playback changes that scale. The editing selection has a dim indicator when it differs from the applied scale. [Scale locks](#scale-locks) can be set to apply a scale globally or to a single channel, activating at a designated step. Global locks persist until another global lock or the global scale track wraps. Channel-lock duration follows the Scales Lock Until Pattern End option. To set a scale lock, hold a step and press the desired scale slot button. On the scale page, this applies globally to all channels without an active channel scale trig lock; on a channel's page, it applies as a channel scale trig lock, affecting only that channel. Channel-specific scale locks override global scales and locks. You can also adjust the rate of the global scale track and set its length independently of other channels, enabling chord progressions that extend beyond a single pattern. This feature offers substantial flexibility for crafting intricate chord progressions and varying patterns.

Scale editor demo

controls.gesture: Press Grid (4, 8).
controls.result: The Scale Editor opens. Scale slots are the 16 buttons on Grid row 3.

controls.gesture: Short-press a scale slot on row 3.
controls.result: Apply it globally and select it for editing. Press the applied slot again to turn global scale off while it stays selected for editing.

controls.gesture: Hold K1 and press a scale slot, or long-press a different editing slot.
controls.result: Select the slot for editing without changing which scale playback uses.

controls.gesture: Long-press the slot already selected for editing.
controls.result: Turn global scale off and clear the editing selection.

controls.gesture: On the Scale screen, turn E2 to select Root, Scale, Degree, Transpose or Rotation. Turn E3 to change its value.
controls.result: The value changes in the draft for the slot named in the title row. Nothing sounds different yet.

controls.gesture: Release all grid keys, then press K3 or K2.
controls.result: K3 applies the draft. K2 cancels it. Applying changes to a scale used by playback changes its harmony immediately.

controls.gesture: On the Scale clock task, turn E2 to Rate and E3 to the rate, then press K3.
controls.result: Set the rate of the global scale track. Selected range, Global cap and Playable range are shown for reference and cannot be edited there.

controls.gesture: On the Scale page, hold the first step of a range on the scale track and press its last step.
controls.result: Set the length of the scale track independently of the channels. The tooltip reads Channel 17 length changed.

controls.gesture: Hold a sequencer step, then press a scale slot.
controls.result: Set or toggle a scale lock at that step: global on the Scale page, channel-specific on a channel page.

Selecting a slot for editing does not switch playback to it; however, saving changes to a scale already used by playback changes that scale. The editing selection has a dim indicator when it differs from the applied scale.

[Scale locks](#scale-locks) can be set to apply a scale globally or to a single channel, activating at a designated step. Global locks persist until another global lock or the global scale track wraps. Channel-lock duration follows the Scales Lock Until Pattern End option. To set a scale lock, hold a step and press the desired scale slot button. On the scale page, this applies globally to all channels without an active channel scale trig lock; on a channel's page, it applies as a channel scale trig lock, affecting only that channel. Channel-specific scale locks override global scales and locks.

details.title: Editing selection and applied scale
details.text: The title row names the slot selected for editing. The editing indicator is dim when that slot differs from the applied scale. With global scale off and no scale lock, pattern degrees play as chromatic semitone offsets. An active channel scale lock takes precedence over the global scale.

details.title: Vertical list controls
details.text: Scale settings appear as vertical rows. Turn E2 to select a row and bring later fields into view. E3 edits the selected slot's draft; K3 applies it and K2 cancels it. Selecting another row does not apply a draft. Tapping a grid key, including Play/Stop, cancels an unapplied draft, so press K3 before using the grid to keep your edit. A long scale name uses a separate full-width value row.

details.title: Scale lock lifetime
details.text: A global scale lock lasts until another global lock or until the global scale track wraps. A channel scale lock follows PARAMS > MOSAIC > Scales lock until ptn end, which is On by default. See Scale Locks.

details.title: Scale clock and Overview
details.text: Scale clock sets the rate of the global scale track. Overview is a read-only dashboard: it lists the playing scale, the scale being edited, the step range, the transposition and any step lock. Both are Scale tasks beside Scale.

recipes.title: Prepare and apply a second scale
recipes.text:
Start with a channel that plays a four-step melody on pattern degrees 1 to 4 (see [Build a phrase](#build-a-phrase)) and scale slot 1 applied as C major. The melody sounds MIDI 60, 62, 64 and 65 (C, D, E, F). The captured examples below start from the same setup: Save D major, then apply it follows steps 1 to 5, and Prepare a scale before applying it adds browsing a slot with a long press, editing the applied slot and turning the global scale Off.

1. Press Grid (4, 8) to open the Scale Editor. Slot 1, the left button on row 3, is bright.

2. Hold K1, press slot 2 at (2, 3), then release both. The title row names slot 2 and a dim indicator marks it. Playback is still in C major.

3. Turn E2 to Root and turn E3 two clicks to D. Release all grid keys and press K3. The draft is saved to slot 2. Tap Play (1,8), listen, then tap Stop: the melody still plays C, D, E, F because slot 1 is still applied.

4. Short-press slot 2 at (2, 3). It becomes the bright applied slot. Tap Play (1,8), listen, then tap Stop: the melody plays D, E, F sharp, G (MIDI 62, 64, 66, 67). The rhythm has not changed.

5. Short-press slot 1 at (1, 3), tap Play and listen: C, D, E, F are restored.

details.text: The current global value, or the persistent step-lock value, is added to the active scale slot's Transpose value. For its lifetime, a step lock replaces the global fader value.

details.title: Each Song slot has its own transposition
details.text: Transposition belongs to the selected Song Sequence. Copying a Song slot copies its transposition, and changing the copy leaves the original as it was.

details.title: Edits during playback
details.text: A change made while notes sound does not cut the sounding note or change its length. The next onset uses the new value. In the captured example, +1 and then -12 raise the following notes by one semitone and then drop them an octave from the written pitch.

recipes.title: Play a copied Song slot a tone higher
recipes.text:
This recipe changes the transposition fader on a copy of a slot, so the copy plays a tone higher while the original stays put. It is a different workflow from the captured example below, which shows the fader being pressed while a note is sounding.

Start with Song slot 1 holding a finished sequence, such as a four-note melody on MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65, with playback stopped and Song mode at its default (On).

1. Press Grid (6, 8) to open the Song Editor. Slot 1 at (1, 1) is lit: it is the slot you are working on.

2. Hold slot 1 at (1, 1) and press slot 2 at (2, 1), then release both. Slot 2 now holds a copy of slot 1 (copying overwrites whatever slot 2 held).

3. Press slot 2 at (2, 1) to select it while stopped.

4. Press Grid (4, 8) to open the Scale Editor.

5. Press the right end of the transposition fader, (16, 8), twice. Each press adds one semitone and the tooltip shows Transpose: 2.

6. Press Play. Slot 2 plays 62, 64, 66, 67. With Song mode On, playback moves on to the next slot after the repeats set in Slot setup; to hold on one slot, open PARAMS > MOSAIC and turn Song mode Off (E3). Press Stop.

7. Press Grid (6, 8), then slot 1 at (1, 1), and press Play to hear the original at 60, 62, 64, 65, because slot 1 kept its transposition of 0.

Check that the raised notes are still inside the usable range of the sound you are playing.

details.title: Song slot contents
details.text: Copying a Song slot copies its sequence configuration. Source note patterns and channel settings can be reused or changed within the copied slot.

recipes.title: Create a two-slot group
recipes.text:
Starting point: slot 1 holds a four-step motif on channel 1 (C D E F, MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; build it as in Creating a First Loop), playback is stopped and Song mode is On (the default; Song Playback shows it as AUTO). Slots 2 and 3 are empty and dim at (2,1) and (3,1).

1. Press Song (6,8). Slot 1 at (1,1) is bright because it is selected. A slot plays 64 steps by default, about eleven seconds at 90 BPM with Rate /1, so shorten the audition first: tap (2,7) to set the global length to 1 step, then tap (8,7) three times to make it 4 steps. The length belongs to the slot, so the copy in step 2 keeps it.

2. Hold slot 1 at (1,1), press slot 2 at (2,1), then release both. Slot 2 turns mid-bright: it is a full copy of slot 1.

3. Tap slot 2 at (2,1). It turns bright and slot 1 drops to mid-bright.

4. Press Channel (3,8), tap channel 1 at (1,1) and tap octave +1 at (11,8). Slot 2 now plays the motif an octave higher. Slot 1 is unchanged. Change a rhythm or a mask instead of the octave if you prefer.

5. Press Song (6,8) and look at slot 3 at (3,1). It stays dim because it is empty, and an empty slot ends the group after slot 2.

6. Tap slot 1 at (1,1) and press Play (1,8). Slot 1 plays the motif (60, 62, 64, 65), then slot 2 plays it an octave higher (72, 74, 76, 77), then playback returns to slot 1 and repeats.

Each slot plays for its global length times its Repeats, so with the length left at 64 a slot lasts about eleven seconds. Check or change Song mode in Song tasks > Slot setup (see Song Mode Operations). The captured example Loop a song group or hold one slot, below, plays two groups built this way (slots 1-2 and 4-5) and what happens when Song mode is turned Off.

details.title: Copy direction
details.text: Press the source slot first, then the destination. Either release order uses the first-pressed slot as the source. Copying leaves the source and other slots unchanged.

recipes.title: Copy a slot before editing
recipes.text:
Starting point: slot 1 holds a section you want to keep, for example the four-note motif C D E F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65). Playback is stopped and the Song editor is open (Song, grid (6,8)).

1. Hold slot 1 at (1,1). While holding it, press an empty slot, slot 2 at (2,1). Release both. Slot 2 changes from dim to mid-bright: it is a full copy and slot 1 is untouched. Copying overwrites the destination, so choose an empty one.

2. Tap slot 2 at (2,1). It turns bright (selected) and slot 1 drops to mid-bright.

3. Edit the variation while stopped: press Channel (3,8), tap channel 1 at (1,1) and tap octave +1 at (11,8). Only slot 2 changes. (Changing a mask instead works too; either edit stays in the selected slot.)

4. Press Play (1,8). Slot 2 plays the motif an octave higher (72, 74, 76, 77); with Song mode On playback then carries on to slot 1, so press Stop when you have heard enough. Press Song (6,8), tap slot 1 at (1,1) and press Play: the original section still plays 60, 62, 64, 65. Tap slot 2 to compare.

The destination is a full copy, so editing it never changes the original. To erase a slot you no longer need, hold an empty slot and press the slot to clear. There is no undo. The captured example [Copy a slot, then change the copy](#song-mode-operations/song-copy-and-compare) shows steps 1 to 3 (the copy and the octave edit); to hear slot 1 and slot 2 compare, follow [Build two song groups](#song-mode-operations/song-build-two-groups), which plays the copies. The captured example [Read Song slot lights](#button-indicators/song-slot-light-states) shows the lights for a copy and for the erase.

features.title: Song Mode Operations

readme.excerpt: When "song mode" is activated, the sequencer automatically progresses to the next slot after a pattern has played its designated number of repetitions. If it encounters an empty slot, it loops back to the first filled slot within that sequence, facilitating smooth transitions between unique pattern groups. If you wish to change slots during playback, the sequencer will queue your command and execute it after the current sequence completes.

details.title: Song groups
details.text: When the next slot is empty, playback returns to the first filled slot of the current contiguous group. Manual slot selection remains available when Song mode is off.

details.title: How long a slot lasts
details.text: A slot plays its global length in steps, once for every repeat, before Song mode advances. Set the length with the fader on row 7 and Repeats in Slot setup.

recipes.title: Create two Song groups
recipes.text:
Starting point: channel 1 plays its default four-note motif (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) on slot 1, the first slot. Song mode is On (the default) and playback is stopped. Group A will be slots 1-2 and group B slots 4-5. Slots 3 and 6 stay empty.

1. Set the length: press Song (6,8) with slot 1 selected. Tap (2,7), which sets the global length to 1 step, then tap (8,7) once to add one step. The length is now 2 steps, so each slot plays only the first two notes, 60 and 62.

2. Copy slot 1 to slots 2, 4 and 5: hold slot 1 at (1,1) and press slot 2 at (2,1). Repeat for slot 4 at (4,1) and slot 5 at (5,1). The copies keep the two-step length.

3. Voice slot 2: tap slot 2 at (2,1), press Channel (3,8), tap channel 1 at (1,1) and tap octave +1 at (11,8). Slot 2 will play 72, 74.

4. Voice slot 4: press Song (6,8), tap slot 4 at (4,1), press Channel (3,8), tap channel 1 at (1,1) and tap octave +2 at (12,8). Slot 4 will play 84, 86.

5. Voice slot 5 the same way: Song (6,8), slot 5 at (5,1), Channel (3,8), channel 1 at (1,1) and octave -1 at (9,8). Slot 5 will play 48, 50.

6. Check the lights: slots 1, 2, 4 and 5 are mid-bright, slots 3 and 6 are dim and the selected slot is bright.

7. Tap slot 1 at (1,1) and press Play (1,8). Group A loops: slot 1 plays 60, 62, slot 2 plays 72, 74, then empty slot 3 sends playback back to slot 1.

8. While slot 1 sounds, tap slot 4 at (4,1). It blinks, queued. When slot 1 finishes, group B plays: slot 4 plays 84, 86, slot 5 plays 48, 50, then empty slot 6 returns playback to the first slot of group B. To go back, tap slot 1 or slot 2 to queue a return to group A.

For a more musical version, replace the octave edits with a different bass rhythm or harmony in group B and keep one motif in both groups. The captured examples below build these slots: Build two song groups follows steps 1 to 7, up to the first group looping, and Loop a song group or hold one slot builds the same slots and goes on to the second group and queued selection (step 8).

features.title: Adjusting Song Sequence Length

readme.excerpt:
The song sequence's length can be adjusted using the fader located at the lower left of the song editor page. * The global length can be set anywhere from 1 step to 64 step, offering a wide range of possibilities. * Channel start and end steps can be outside of the range of the global length, but channels length cannot exceed overal global length. The cap counts steps from the channel start: a channel set to steps 2–4 with global length 2 plays steps 2 and 3 repeatedly. Increasing the global length restores the remaining selected steps. This also applies to the scale track and follows each track’s clock rate; explicit song reset options still apply.

Global pattern length demo

details.title: Global length and channel range
details.text: With channel range 2–4 and global length 2, the channel repeats steps 2 and 3. Its selected endpoint remains at 4. Increasing global length restores step 4. The scale track follows the same length cap. Each track retains its clock rate, and explicit song reset options still apply.

recipes.title: Shorten and restore a phrase
recipes.text:
Starting point: channel 1 plays a four-step motif on steps 1 to 4 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65). Its channel range is steps 1 to 4 and the global length is 64 steps. Playback is stopped.
1. Press Song (6,8). The length fader is on row 7, columns 1 to 8.
2. Tap (2,7) to set the global length to one step (the buttons between the ends jump to 1, 13, 32, 38, 51 and 64), then tap (8,7) once to add one step. Song Playback shows Global length reading two.
3. Press Play (1,8). Only the first two steps play: MIDI 60, 62, 60, 62 and so on. The channel range is still steps 1 to 4, so nothing is deleted.
4. Press Stop (1,8). Tap (8,7) twice to set the global length to four steps, then press Play. All four steps return: 60, 62, 64, 65.
Use this to loop a short fragment of a longer motif without editing it, then restore the full phrase. The end buttons (1,7) and (8,7) change the length one step at a time. The captured example Set the global song length, below, uses the two end buttons on the Song Playback screen: it takes one step off 64 (63) and puts it back. It does not play, so follow steps 2 to 4 to hear the effect.

features.title: Navigating the Norns Display

readme.excerpt:
The Song page opens on **Playback**, which shows on one screen the playing slot, the one that comes next, the pass within its repeats, the global pattern length and whether song mode is advancing. Choose the other screens from Song tasks (E1).

**Slot setup**: Here, you can set the number of repetitions for each Song Sequence. This setting dictates how sequences transition in song mode. When song mode is off, you manually control slot activation, allowing you to dictate the flow of your song.
**Tempo and feel**: Set the tempo to match the mood you want, from a soothing lullaby to a fast-paced track, and the global swing or shuffle.

controls.result: Edit global tempo and Swing or Shuffle settings. Choose a field with E2, change it with E3, then apply with K3 or cancel with K2.

features.title: Locks

readme.excerpt: Trig param values, masks, and various grid functions can be fixed to specific steps on both the channel and global scale pages of Mosaic. A lock takes effect at its designated step. Its duration depends on the lock type: parameter and octave locks affect that step, while scale locks follow the persistence rules below. See the relevant lock section for transposition behaviour. Locks are set on the channel edit page. Trig locks enhance your control over the sequencing process, allowing for precise adjustments and modifications at any step of your sequence.

controls.result: The screen shows the channel default again. The lock remains on the step.

controls.gesture: Hold the step and press K2 on the screen where the lock was set.
controls.result: The lock is removed and the step uses the channel default again.

features.title: Trig Param Locks

readme.excerpt:
Device parameters can be locked on a per-step basis. To set a param trig lock: 1. Hold down the step you want to modify on the channel page sequencer. 2. Adjust the param value that you want to lock to this step. To clear parameter trig locks from a specific step: 1. On the channel editor, show Trig params on the Norns screen (Channel tasks, E1). 2. Hold the step with trig locks and press K2. To clear all parameter trig locks from a channel: 1. Ensure you are on the trig lock page on your norns device. 2. Hold shift (K1). 3. Press K2.

Trig locks demo

recipes.title: Brighten the last note with a cutoff lock
recipes.text:
Start with a channel that has trigs on steps 1 to 4 (see Build a phrase), sends to a device that lists a controller you can hear on a filter, and is stopped. This recipe uses CC 74, the usual filter cutoff controller: a generic CC device lists it as CC 74, and a device whose configuration names it shows it as Cutoff. The scenes on this page use CC 1 the same way.
1. Open Trig params: turn E1 to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Trig params, press K3.
2. Turn E2 to slot 1, press K2, turn E3 to CC 74 (Cutoff), press K3 to assign it, then press K2 to return to the slot view.
3. With no step held, turn E3 to 40, the channel default: every step sends CC 74 = 40 before its note.
4. Hold step 4, the last trig, and turn E3 to 100 (the cell shows 100 and the L marker). Release step 4 and the cell shows 40 again.
5. Press Play. Steps 1 to 3 sound with cutoff 40 and step 4 sends CC 74 = 100 just before its note, so the last note of each loop is brighter.
6. To remove the accent, hold step 4 and press K2.
On this page, the scene Lock a value, then clear just that step shows the same gestures with Fixed Note, the MIDI strip of Use the first and last Trig params slots shows CC values arriving just before their notes, and Keep a stored value while locking a step shows one locked CC value ahead of a step's note while the other steps send the stored value. For a smooth rise instead of a jump, see Param Slides.

features.title: Param Slides

readme.excerpt:
To enable parameter slides for a trig parameter, select the desired parameter and press K3. This will activate parameter slides for every trig lock of this type on the channel. While enabled, locks will smoothly transition between each other. Note that transitions do not transition across song patterns but can wrap within the same pattern if the Param Slide Wrap setting is enabled. Use this sparingly as it is resource intensive To lock a parameter slide to a specific step: - Hold down the desired step. - Press K3 on the chosen trig parameter. This locks the parameter slide to the selected step, causing it to transition smoothly to the next lock. All other locks remain unaffected.

Param slides demo

recipes.title: Open a filter over two steps
recipes.text:
Start with a channel with trigs on steps 1 to 4, a controller assigned to a Trig params slot (CC 1 as in the scenes, or the CC that drives your filter), and playback stopped (see the Brighten the last note recipe on Trig Param Locks).
1. Open Trig params and turn E2 to that slot.
2. Hold step 1, turn E3 to 24 and release. Hold step 3, turn E3 to 96 and release.
3. Release all steps and press K3. The cell shows S. Press Play: the value leaves 24 at step 1 and reaches 96 as step 3's note starts (the CC strip in the scene lists 36, 48, 60, 72, 84, 96). Press Play again to stop.
4. To slide only the first lock, first add a third lock: hold step 4, turn E3 to 48 and release. Press K3 with no step held to switch the channel-wide slide off, then hold step 1 and press K3 (the cell shows S while step 1 is held). Press Play: 24 glides to 96 between steps 1 and 3, then jumps to 48 at step 4. With only two locks, a slide on step 1 alone and a slide on every lock sound the same; the third lock is what separates them. Stop.
5. To loop the sweep, open PARAMS > MOSAIC and turn Wrap param slides On.
6. Release all steps and press K3 to switch the channel-wide slide on again. The last lock, step 4, now slides back towards 24 across the loop boundary instead of holding at 48.

features.title: Scale Locks

readme.excerpt:
Scales can be set on a per-step basis. They can be set globally across all channels on the Scale Editor, or per channel oin the Channel Editor. Scale locks set on steps in the Channel Editor take precedence over global scale locks. With Scales Lock Until Pattern End on, a channel scale lock persists until that channel wraps to its start, unless another channel scale lock replaces it. With the option off, it persists until the next active trig that passes its probability check; a probability-rejected trig does not clear it. A scale lock on that next trig applies in place of the old lock. Global scale-track locks are independent of this option: they persist until another global lock replaces them or the global scale track wraps. To set a scale lock: 1. Hold down the step you want to modify on the channel page sequencer. 2. Press the desired scale slot. To clear a grid trig lock: 1. Hold the step with the locked value. 2. Press K2.

Scale locks demo

features.title: Save and Load

readme.excerpt:
You can save and load your creations using the param menu. When you choose to save, you'll be prompted to enter a name for your creation. Remember to use a descriptive name so you can easily find and manage your projects.

The sequencer features an autosave function when it is not actively playing. If left idle, it will automatically save your work under the name "autosave" after 60 seconds. When you start Mosaic again, it automatically loads this most recent autosave. Before replacing the current project, Mosaic checks saved song slots, global lengths, and channel and scale-track ranges. If a check fails, the screen identifies the problem and the current project and playback are retained. Autosaving is then suspended to protect the rejected file; editing, playing or cancelling a dialog does not resume it. Successfully loading a valid project, saving a named project, or choosing New resumes the normal idle autosave interval. A failed save leaves autosaving suspended. Valid saved one-step ranges remain supported, without adding a one-step range gesture. These checks cover the saved range structure, not every possible corrupted project field.

To ensure the longevity of your work, it's important to save your creations into named slots. This prevents them from being overwritten by the autosave feature, allowing you to keep your songs indefinitely.

recipes.title: Prepare Mosaic for a live set
recipes.text:
1. Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC.
2. Select Shift press to stop and turn E3 to On, so a stray tap cannot stop the sequencer.
3. Press K2, then K1, and start playback with Play/Stop at grid (1,8). A quick second tap is ignored, and so is a hold shorter than one second.
4. To stop, hold K1 and tap Play/Stop, or hold Play/Stop for one second or more. Shift press stop lists every stop gesture.
5. Leave Song mode On, its default, if the arrangement should advance on its own. [Decide whether a slow channel restarts](#reset-at-pattern-repeat/repeat-reset-policies) turns Song mode Off to show the difference, and [Set Song slot repetitions](#navigating-the-norns-display/song-slot-repeat-values) shows Song mode in Slot setup. The other option groups are described below.

details.title: Which lesson to read
details.text: Stopping safely: Shift press stop. Song sections: Song mode and the two reset options, read in that order. Slides across the loop end: Parameter slides wrap. Syncing a pattern-based receiver: Elektron program changes.

recipes.title: Arrange sections that restart together
recipes.text:
1. Hold step 1 on the Channel editor and tap step 3 to give channel 1 a three-step range, shorter than the 64-step slot. In the Song editor (grid (6,8)) hold slot 1 at (1,1) and tap slot 2 at (2,1) to copy it, so the song has two slots.
2. Open PARAMS > MOSAIC. Leave Song mode On and Reset on song seq change On, close the menu and press Play. Watch the slot LEDs: slot 1 is bright.
3. After 10.7 seconds (64 steps at 90 BPM) the LEDs swap to slot 2. Because the reset is On, channel 1 starts its three-step line again on its first step at that moment, so it lines up with the section at every change.
4. Stop, turn Reset on song seq change Off and play again. The three-step line now carries on across the change and drifts against the sections, which is the right choice for evolving polyrhythms.

recipes.title: Rehearse one section
recipes.text:
Starting point: Song mode is On (the default) and the song has two filled slots, slot 1 and slot 2, so it would normally play 1, 2, 1, 2 and so on. Playback is stopped.

1. Open PARAMS > MOSAIC (tap K1), select Song mode and turn E3 to Off.

2. Press Song (6,8) to open the Song editor. The slots are the buttons on rows 1 to 6; slot 1 is (1,1) and slot 2 is (2,1). Tap the slot you want to rehearse, for example slot 1 at (1,1).

3. Press Play at (1,8). The slot repeats: with Song mode Off it never moves on to slot 2 by itself, so you hear the same section again and again.

4. To move to another section, tap its slot, for example (2,1) while the music plays. The press is queued and takes over when the current pass ends. Turn Song mode On again to run the whole arrangement.

For comparison, with Song mode On the same two slots play 1, 2, 1, 2. The captured example [Loop a song group or hold one slot](#song-mode-operations/song-mode-groups-and-selection) shows both: with Song mode On a group of slots loops, and with Song mode Off slot 1 repeats (60, 62, 60, 62) and a manual selection of slot 2 still takes over at the end of the pass.

recipes.title: Hear the section restart
recipes.text:
Start from channel 1's four-note pattern, C D E F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65), and leave the song's global length at its default of 64 steps.

recipes.title: Sweep a filter around the loop
recipes.text:
Start with a stopped channel with trigs on steps 1 to 4 and Wrap param slides Off (its default) in PARAMS > MOSAIC.
1. Open Trig params: turn E1 to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Trig params, press K3. Press K2, turn E3 to CC 1 (or the CC that drives your filter), press K3 to assign it and K2 to return.
2. Hold step 1 and turn E3 to 24, release; hold step 3 and turn E3 to 96, release; hold step 4 and turn E3 to 48, release. Step 2 has no lock, so it sends only the channel default (the scenes store 63).
3. Hold step 4 and press K3 to give that last lock a slide.
4. Press Play and let it loop. On a MIDI monitor, or in the MIDI strip of the scene Carry a slide across the loop boundary, CC 1 holds 48 from step 4 and then jumps to 24 at the loop point. Stop.
5. Open PARAMS > MOSAIC, select Wrap param slides and turn E3 to On, then Play again. CC 1 now glides from 48 through 40 and 32 to 24 across one step and arrives with the first note.

features.title: Scales Lock Until Pattern End

readme.excerpt: The "Scales lock until ptn end" option is on by default and controls channel scale locks. When on, a lock persists until the channel wraps to its start, unless another channel scale lock replaces it. When off, the next active trig that passes its probability check clears the previous lock; probability-rejected trigs do not clear it. A new lock on that trig takes effect normally. Global scale-track locks do not use this option: they persist until replacement or global-track wrap.

recipes.title: Hear every note restricted
recipes.text:
Use this option to keep generated, random or merged material consonant: with Lock all to pent. On, every note lands on the five-note version of the scale. The seven-note walk below is a diagnostic rather than a phrase, so you can hear exactly which degrees are replaced. Starting point: channel 1 plays pattern 1 (C, D, E, F on steps 1 to 4) in C major.

1. Build seven degrees. Press Pattern (5,8), select pattern 1 (1,1) and tap trigs on steps 5, 6 and 7 at (5,4), (6,4) and (7,4). Press Pattern (5,8) again for the note page and tap (5,3), (6,2) and (7,1) to put steps 5 to 7 on degrees V, VI and VII: steps 1 to 7 now form a rising diagonal.

2. Set the range. Press Channel (3,8), hold step 1 (1,4), tap step 7 (7,4) and release both. Tap Play (1,8) and listen: 60, 62, 64, 65, 67, 69, 71. Tap Play to stop.

3. Restrict the notes. Tap K1, open PARAMS > MOSAIC, select Lock all to pent. and turn E3 to On. Close the menu and tap Play: 60, 62, 64, 64, 67, 69, 72. F falls to E and B rises to C because only C D E G A are allowed. Tap Play to stop.

4. Change the scale. Open the Scale Editor (4,8), turn E3 to another scale, press K3 and return to Channel (3,8). Play again: each scale has its own five notes. Natural minor, for example, gives 60, 63, 63, 65, 67, 67, 70.

5. Turn the option Off in PARAMS > MOSAIC to restore all seven degrees of the current scale.

recipes.title: Compare random notes with and without the filter
recipes.text:
Lock random to pent. is On by default. This recipe lets you hear what it does by switching it Off and On with Random Note at 4. Random Note chooses its offsets at random, so listen to several loops: a short run may not include every note.

Starting point: channel 1 plays pattern 1 (C, D, E, F on steps 1 to 4) in C major; no Trig params slot is assigned yet.

1. Assign Random Note. Select channel 1 and press E1 to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Trig params and press K3. Press K2 to open the parameter list, turn E3 to Random Note, press K3 to assign it to the first slot and press K2 to return. The slot reads 0 and the pattern still plays C, D, E, F.

2. Set the amount. With the Random Note slot selected (E2), turn E3 four detents right to 4. Each note is now offset by -2, -1, 0, +1 or +2 scale degrees at random. A step that draws offset 0 keeps its own note.

3. Open PARAMS > MOSAIC, select Lock random to pent. and turn E3 to Off. Close the menu, tap Play and listen to several loops: F and B join the random notes, and one of them will turn up within a few passes. Tap Play to stop.

4. Turn Lock random to pent. On and play several loops again. The random notes now stay on C, D, E, G and A. A step that draws offset 0 keeps its own note, so a plain F in the pattern can still sound. The random stream is not reset between the two runs, so the two runs will not start with the same notes; compare which notes occur, not the order.

features.title: Lock Merged to Pentatonic

readme.excerpt: Similarly, "Lock merged to pent." is on by default and ensures notes modified by merge modes stick to the pentatonic version of the currently selected scale. Mosaic uses these application-specific five-note selections (one-based degrees of each named seven-note scale): Major and Harmonic Major 1/2/3/5/6; Minor, Harmonic Minor and Melodic Minor 1/3/4/5/7; Dorian 1/2/4/5/7; Phrygian 1/3/4/6/7; Lydian 2/3/5/6/7; Mixolydian 1/2/4/5/6; Locrian 2/3/4/6/7. The named scale’s alterations apply; these selections do not always retain the tonic or avoid semitones. Merged values remain seven-note scale degrees, not five-note indices. Their scale pitches snap to the nearest selected pitch repeated across octaves, choosing the lower pitch on an exact tie; snapping may cross an octave boundary. For example, Lydian C snaps to the B below it, while Melodic Minor A snaps down to G rather than equally distant B. The scale root is used when set, otherwise the song root, with the effective octave offset applied afterward.

recipes.title: Compare merged notes with and without the filter
recipes.text:
Lock merged to pent. is On by default. Merge modes can produce notes that no pattern contains, such as an average between two degrees; this option snaps those results onto the five-note version of the scale. Use this recipe to hear the difference.

Starting point: channel 1 is empty and the scale is C major.

1. Build pattern 1 on degrees I, III, V, VII (C E G B) on steps 1 to 4 and pattern 2 on III, V, VII, I (E G B C) on steps 1 to 4, as in Build a phrase, and pattern 3 as a velocity source (four trigs on steps 1 to 4, never assigned to the channel). Both note patterns have a trig on all four steps.

2. Assign both patterns to channel 1 with (1,2) and (2,2).

3. Choose the merge modes. Both patterns trig on the same steps, and the default trig merge, Skip, silences steps that trig in more than one pattern, so set the trig merge to All: press the trig merge button (14,8) until Channel tasks > Merge modes shows ALL. Check that the note merge reads AVERAGE; the average of each pair of degrees is II, IV, VI, IV (D, F, A, F).

4. Open PARAMS > MOSAIC, select Lock merged to pent. and turn E3 to Off. Tap Play: 62, 65, 69, 65 (D, F, A, F). Tap Play to stop.

5. Turn Lock merged to pent. On and play again: 62, 64, 69, 64. The two F notes become E, because F is not in the pentatonic.

recipes.title: Play a minor scale on the white keys
recipes.text:
Starting point: a MIDI keyboard is connected to Mosaic's MIDI input on port 1, channel 1 has a device selected (it plays through the test or your own synth) and the scale is C major. The norns names MIDI 60 as C3, so the key you call middle C sounds 60.

1. Open PARAMS > MOSAIC > Midi control, turn E2 to Map scale to white keys and turn E3 to On. Play the white keys from C to C: C major, 60, 62, 64, 65, 67, 69, 71, 72, the same pitches as before. Each black key repeats the white key above it.

2. Open the Scale Editor (4,8). Turn E2 to Scale, turn E3 to natural minor and press K3 to apply it. Return to the Channel editor (3,8).

3. Play C to C on the white keys again: 60, 62, 63, 65, 67, 68, 70, 72. The keyboard keeps its layout while the scale underneath it has changed.

features.title: UI Motion

readme.excerpt: Turns decorative screen motion on or off (**PARAMS > MOSAIC > UI motion**, default On): the start-up animation, the light running round _Mosaic_'s mark, the selection's shadow gliding across the Masks and Trig params grids (diagonally when it changes row), names and values too long for their space scrolling right to left so you can read them in full (the names in the Masks and Trig params grids stay still), values rolling into place, and the characters. The Rhythm Doctor dances to the tempo of the captured bank, the Merge Shape garden sways and the Harmony choir bobs while the sequencer plays, and a metronome swings on the clock and tempo screens. A single numeric value, such as a mask or trig param, also shows a small dial of where it sits in its range, beside the value itself. Motion never delays input, hides a value for more than a moment or changes timing; with it off, every screen is still.

controls.gesture: Open PARAMS > MOSAIC. Select UI motion. Change its value.
controls.result: Off keeps the screen still; On enables decorative motion and musical characters without changing input or sequencer timing. Default: On.

recipes.title: Compare the screen with motion Off and On
recipes.text:
Use this to see what the setting does before you film or photograph the display. Changing a value only makes the screen react: the point is the header mark.
1. Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC. Select UI motion in the Screen section and turn E3 to Off.
2. Turn E1 to open Channel tasks, select Clock and press K3. Turn E3 to /1.5 and press K3, then restore /1. All values stay readable and the header mark does not move.
3. Return to PARAMS, set UI motion to On, and repeat. The header mark now animates; values are as readable as before.
4. Play the pattern in each setting. The notes and timing are identical.

features.title: Musical Merge and Voice Leading

readme.excerpt:
Mosaic can reshape a channel's merged rhythm and place its notes into stable
registers without rewriting any source pattern. Both features are optional and
default to Off, so an older project keeps its original MIDI, timing and random
behaviour.

Merge modes, Merge Shape and Harmony are consecutive Channel tasks. Open Merge Shape or Harmony there. Their screens use vertical lists, including Rhythm, Phrase, Pitch and the Harmony settings. Their first screens, Merge
Shape and Voice leading, are lists: each row shows its value or `OPEN >`, and the
chosen row is marked `>`. E2 selects a row, E3 changes a staged value, K3 on a row marked `OPEN >` opens it (the last line names it, for
example `K3 OPEN RHYTHM`), and K3 elsewhere validates and applies the whole draft.
Rows that carry out an action instead, such as Create group, Four-part smooth,
Delete group and Reset map (the last two ask first), keep a plain `>`. K2 discards the draft, or returns from a
row you opened to the one it came from. E1 returns to the first screen of the
feature, discarding an unapplied draft, and from there to Channel tasks. A stopped edit applies immediately. During playback, Merge Shape displays
`NEXT CYCLE` and activates before the next channel-cycle onset; Harmony displays
`NEXT PATTERN` and activates at the next global pattern boundary. Stop makes the
latest applied request active for the next start.

features.title: Merge Shape

readme.excerpt:
![Merge Shape Phrase settings in a vertical list on Norns](images/merge-shape-phrase.png)

![Merge Shape Foundation rhythm settings on Norns](images/merge-shape-foundation.png)

Mode Off uses the saved legacy Skip, Only or All trig merge. While Foundation is on it decides the channel's trigs instead: the Merge modes screen shows the trig mode as `SHAPE (ONLY)` and the grid trig merge button's tooltip says Merge Shape is in use; the saved trig mode applies again when Merge Shape is off. Note, velocity and length merge modes still apply. Foundation selects
one assigned pattern as the protected Anchor. Other assigned trig patterns offer
candidate additions at non-anchor steps; overlaps remain one anchor. Amount
admits a deterministic, seed-ranked subset, Accent scales addition velocity, and
Gap suppresses additions within 0–8 circular channel steps of an anchor. Anchor
velocity remains authored. Explicit channel/step masks still win, probability
can still reject an onset, and source patterns are never flattened or changed.

Phrase Cycles can be 1, 2, 4 or 8. Flat, Build, Answer and Fill are stored as
visible per-cycle percentages; changing a percentage makes a Custom curve.
Fixed repeats the same ranked additions. Per phrase changes ranking only after a
complete phrase. Each channel loop advances its own CYCLE counter—even with
polymetric ranges, swing or mute—and Stop restarts at cycle 1.

Keep anchor pitch uses the anchor pattern's relative note on anchor steps before
normal scale conversion. Addition Target can be Legacy, the full effective
scale, selected effective degree indices, or the immutable material of an enabled
Harmony Ensemble group. Targets affect admitted additions only. Note masks,
random shifts and fixed-note operations keep their existing precedence and show
a bypass rather than being quantised twice. Nearest-note ties choose the lower
pitch. A missing/empty target visibly falls back to the legacy pitch.

Foundation ranking is repeatable for the saved seed and grows as a nested set:
raising Amount cannot remove an already selected addition while source, gap,
seed and phrase are unchanged.

Mode has a third choice, Fragments, and Foundation gains Interlock and
Structure. Each is part of the same draft: K3 applies it (`NEXT CYCLE` while
playing), K2 discards it, and one undo step restores it.

controls.gesture: On Merge modes, select Strategy with E2 and turn E3 to FOUNDATION, or press grid (14,8) until it selects Foundation.

recipes.title: Set a two-cycle Build phrase
recipes.text:
Musical purpose: build a part over two loops. Loop 1 plays the anchor line with one extra note. Loop 2 plays the same line with both extra notes.

Starting point: channel 1 has an 8-step loop at 90 BPM with the default Rate /1, so each step is one sixteenth note (one sixth of a second). Pattern 1 holds C D E F on steps 1 to 4 (velocities 127, 117, 107, 97). Pattern 2 holds a C on steps 5 and 7, and both patterns are assigned to the channel. Strategy is SKIP.

1. Press E1 to open Channel tasks, select Merge Shape with E2 and press K3. The Merge Shape list opens: Strategy, Rhythm, Phrase, Pitch, Result.
2. Select Rhythm with E2 and press K3. The Rhythm list opens with Anchor on the first row.
3. Turn E3 once so Anchor reads 01, then press K3. The footer reads APPLIED. Pattern 1 is now the anchor, so its four trigs always play.
4. Press E1 for Channel tasks, select Merge modes, select Strategy with E2 and turn E3 until it reads FOUNDATION (or press grid (14,8) until it does). Active reads FOUNDATION. The channel grid lights steps 1 to 5 and 7: four anchors and two possible additions.
5. Return to Merge Shape. Select Phrase with E2 and press K3. The Phrase list opens: Cycles, Shape, Variation.
6. Select Cycles and turn E3 once right. Cycles reads 2 and two Cycle rows appear.
7. Select Shape and turn E3 once right, from FLAT to BUILD. Cycle 1 reads 50 and Cycle 2 reads 100, so the first loop admits half of the additions and the second loop admits all of them.
8. Press K3 on a value row. The footer reads APPLIED.
9. Press Play (grid (1,8)) and listen to four loops, then press Stop. Loop 1 plays C D E F and one extra C on step 7; loop 2 plays C D E F and extra Cs on steps 5 and 7; then the two loops repeat. The extra notes play at velocity 70, quieter than the anchors.

What each loop plays (an added C is shown as +C):

Loop 1: steps 1 to 4 C D E F, step 5 rest, step 7 +C.

Loop 2: steps 1 to 4 C D E F, step 5 +C, step 7 +C.

Listen for the loop-to-loop change: the extra C on step 5 is present in every second loop only.

To make the additions quieter or louder without changing how many play, change Add accent in Rhythm.

The captured version of this recipe is [Captured two-cycle Build workflow](#merge-shape/foundation-two-cycle-build).

features.title: Fragments

readme.excerpt:
![Merge Shape Fragments settings on Norns](images/merge-shape-fragments.png)

Fragments is a separate mode for building a phrase from pieces of the assigned
patterns. With Mode set to Fragments, Rhythm opens the Fragments screen: Size (4,
8 or 16 steps), Keep anchor, Anchor (shown only with Keep anchor) and Seed. The
channel loop is cut into fragments of Size steps counted from the channel's own
start step; the last fragment is shorter when the loop does not divide evenly,
and a loop shorter than Size is one fragment. Fragments never cross the loop end.

Each fragment plays one assigned pattern, chosen repeatably by the Seed: the
same seed always gives the same choice. The fragment keeps that pattern's own
trigs, notes, velocities and lengths exactly, so the legacy trig, note,
velocity and length merge modes and merged-pentatonic do not apply while
Fragments is on. The Merge modes screen shows each saved mode as, for example,
`FRAGMENTS (AVERAGE)`, and a merge button's tooltip says Fragments is in use; the
saved modes apply again when Merge Shape is off. A note longer than the gap to
the next onset on the loop is shortened to that gap. Keep anchor also plays the
Anchor pattern's trigs where the fragment's own pattern has none; where both have
a trig, the fragment's pattern wins. With no assigned pattern the mode falls back
to legacy merging and Result says `ASSIGN PATTERN`.

Phrase shows only Cycles and Variation in this mode. Fixed repeats the same
fragment sources every phrase; Per phrase draws new ones for each phrase.
Shape percentages, Amount, Accent and Gap do not apply. Fragments hides Pitch; choose the adjacent Harmony task directly for voice leading. Explicit masks still win and probability can still reject an
onset. The channel grid shows exactly the trigs the fragments play.

recipes.title: Set four-step fragments
recipes.text:
Musical purpose: build one phrase from two patterns, taking the first half of the loop from one pattern and the second half from the other. Each half keeps its source notes and velocities.

Starting point: channel 1 has an 8-step loop at 90 BPM and Rate /1. Pattern 1 holds C D E F on steps 1 to 4 (velocities 127, 117, 107, 97). Pattern 2 holds a C at velocity 100 on steps 3 and 6, and both are assigned to the channel. Strategy is SKIP.

1. Press E1 to open Channel tasks, select Merge modes and press K3. Select Strategy with E2 and turn E3 until it reads FRAGMENTS. Active reads FRAGMENTS. A strategy choice applies at once and needs no K3.
2. Press E1 for Channel tasks, select Merge Shape and press K3. Select Rhythm with E2 and press K3. The Fragments list opens: Size 8, Keep anchor OFF, Seed 0; edits on this list are drafts until you press K3.
3. Select Size and turn E3 once left. Size reads 4, so the loop is cut into two fragments: steps 1 to 4 and steps 5 to 8.
4. Press K3. The footer reads APPLIED and the channel grid lights only step 3, because Seed 0 gives the first fragment to Pattern 2 and the second to Pattern 1, and Pattern 1 has no trigs in the second half.
5. Press Play (grid (1,8)), listen to two loops and press Stop. Each loop plays a single C (MIDI 60) at velocity 100, and Pattern 1’s E on step 3 is not mixed in.
6. Select Seed with E2 and turn E3 once right. Seed reads 1, and a seed always makes the same choice, so Seed 1 gives the first fragment to Pattern 1 and the second to Pattern 2.
7. Press K3. The footer reads APPLIED and the grid lights steps 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6.
8. Press Play. Each loop plays C D E F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) and then Pattern 2’s C on step 6 at velocity 100, then press Stop.

Edits stay drafts until K3, so change Size and Seed first and apply once if you prefer. Turn Keep anchor ON to let the anchor pattern fill empty positions. Open Phrase and set Variation to Per phrase if you want new sources each phrase.

The seed is a repeatable dice roll: seed 0 and seed 1 above give opposite choices for the two halves, and every other seed gives its own choice that always repeats. Try a few more seeds and keep the one you like.

The captured version of this recipe is [Captured Fragments seed and playback workflow](#fragments/fragments-seed-source-choice).

features.title: Interlock

readme.excerpt:
![Merge Shape Interlock settings on Norns](images/merge-shape-interlock.png)

Interlock makes one channel's Foundation additions leave room for another
channel's anchors. On the follower's Rhythm screen, Interlock opens Leader (Off
or any other channel) and Window (0–4 of the follower's steps). An addition is
removed when a leader anchor falls within Window steps of it; Window 0 removes
only additions that start exactly with a leader anchor. Anchors of either channel
are never removed, so an addition removed here simply does not play.

Leader anchors are the anchor pattern's trigs in the leader's loop, planned from
the song, not what the leader happened to sound: probability, mute and swing do
not change them, and swing or shuffle never change which additions are removed.
Channels at different clock divisions or loop lengths are compared in musical
time from Start. The leader must itself use Foundation for its anchors to count;
otherwise Status says `LEADER OFF` or `LEADER MISSING` and nothing is removed.

A channel can follow one leader, and a channel that has a leader cannot be one:
Apply refuses a chain with `LEADER HAS LEADER` or `CHANNEL IS A LEADER` and
keeps your draft. Where Mosaic cannot plan the leader exactly—after a clock
division, loop range or song change while playing (`RESYNC`, until the next
Start or song realign) or beyond its planning budget (`PLAN LIMIT`)—the
follower plays all of its admitted additions for that loop and shows why.
Status on the Interlock screen and the Interlock row on Result show `ON` or the
bypass.

Interlock's planning runs when a follower wraps its loop. On a norns each
follower that wraps on the same step adds about 0.7 ms to that step, so a few
followers wrapping together are inaudible, while every channel following one
leader and wrapping together (15 followers) can make that step land about
10 ms late. Stagger follower loop lengths or wraps if you need very many.

recipes.title: Set Window 0
recipes.text:
Musical purpose: stop one channel’s extra notes landing on another channel’s anchor, for example hi-hat additions that never double the kick. Interlock changes only the follower’s additions. Anchors on both channels always play.

Starting point: Foundation is on for two channels, both with 8-step loops. Channel 1 (the follower, MIDI channel 1) has anchor Pattern 1 (C D E F on steps 1 to 4) and Pattern 2 (a C on steps 5 and 7) as additions. Channel 2 (the leader, MIDI channel 2) has anchor Pattern 3, a single trig on step 5; channel 1 has no leader, and its grid lights steps 1 to 5 and 7.

1. Select channel 1 on the grid (button (1,1)). Press E1 for Channel tasks, select Merge Shape with E2 and press K3.
2. Select Rhythm and press K3, then select Interlock (the last row) and press K3. The Interlock list opens: Leader OFF, Window 0, Status.
3. Select Leader and turn E3 once right. Leader reads CH02. A channel cannot follow itself, so CH01 is not offered.
4. Press K3. The footer reads APPLIED, Window stays 0 and Status reads ON. Step 5 goes dark on the channel 1 grid: Pattern 2’s addition starts exactly on the leader’s anchor and is removed. Steps 1 to 4 and step 7 stay lit.
5. Press Play (grid (1,8)) and listen to two loops, then press Stop. Channel 1 plays steps 1 to 4 and step 7, and channel 2 plays its anchor on step 5; nothing from channel 1 sounds on step 5.
6. Select Window and turn E3 twice right. Window reads 2.
7. Press K3. The footer reads APPLIED. Step 7 also goes dark, because it is two steps from the leader’s anchor on step 5, and only steps 1 to 4 remain on channel 1; if you apply while playing, the footer reads NEXT CYCLE and the change starts at the next loop.

Window 0 removes only additions that start with a leader anchor. Each step of Window widens the gap by one follower step, up to 4.

The captured version of this recipe is [Captured Interlock Leader and Window workflow](#interlock/interlock-leader-window).

features.title: Structure

readme.excerpt:
![Merge Shape Structure settings on Norns](images/merge-shape-structure.png)

Structure snaps chosen moments of a Foundation line to a chord while the notes
in between keep their own pitch. Pitch opens Structure: Markers (Off, Anchors,
Every 4 or Every 8) and Chord group, an enabled Harmony Ensemble group. Anchors
marks every anchor onset; Every 4 and Every 8 mark steps 1, 5, 9… or 1, 9… of the
channel loop counted from its start step. A note at a marker is converted to the
scale as usual and then moved to the nearest pitch class of the group's chord,
taking the lower one on a tie. Notes between markers keep their Addition Target
(additions) or their own pitch (anchors); Mosaic makes no claim that they
resolve. Note masks, random shifts and fixed notes still win at a marker.

Apply needs an enabled group while Markers is on. If the group becomes
unavailable during playback the markers play their ordinary pitch and Result
says `CHORD MISSING`. Deleting or disabling the group turns Markers Off for every
channel that uses it in the same change; Delete group lists those channels first.
During playback that change waits for the next pattern boundary, and a Merge
Shape edit applied to one of those channels before then waits with it and shows
`NEXT PATTERN` instead of `NEXT CYCLE`.
A snapped marker keeps its chord tone when Harmony Revoice or Ensemble would move
it: Harmony's Result says `MARKER PRIORITY`. With Harmony Pattern, a mapped note
value that snaps to a different pitch class at a marker than it plays between
markers has no single mapped pitch, so it is silent at both, whichever fallback
is chosen; unmapped values keep their own pitch.

recipes.title: Snap anchors to a chord, then try Every 4
recipes.text:
Musical purpose: land the strong notes of a line on the tones of a chord while the notes between them stay as written. Anchors snaps every anchor note. Every 4 snaps only steps 1 and 5 of an 8-step loop and leaves the rest of the line alone.

Terms: a Harmony group is a stored chord. Its Template count is how many tones the chord has, each Tone row sets that tone's offset from the root, and Group enabled lets other features use it. Structure moves a marked note to the nearest tone of an enabled group's chord.

Starting point: channel 1 has an 8-step loop with Foundation on. Pattern 1 is the anchor (C D E F on steps 1 to 4, MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65). Pattern 2 supplies additions (a C on steps 5 and 7). If Foundation is not on yet, follow steps 1 to 4 of Set a two-cycle Build phrase first. Steps 1 to 3 build a group that holds the chord C E G; if you already have an enabled group with that chord, start at step 4.

1. Create the group: press E1 for Channel tasks, select Harmony and press K3. Select Groups with E2 and press K3. Select Create group and press K3. Group 1 appears.

2. Set the chord: select Source and press K3. Select Template count and turn E3 twice right, so the chord has 3 tones. Select Tone 2 and turn E3 twice right. Select Tone 3 and turn E3 four times right. With the root, the offsets 2 and 4 are C E G in C major. Press K3 on a value row. The footer reads APPLIED.

3. Enable the group: press K2 to return to Groups. Select Members and press K3, select Group enabled, turn E3 once right to ON and press K3. The footer reads APPLIED. Group 1 is enabled.

4. Open Structure: press E1 for Channel tasks, select Merge Shape and press K3. Select Pitch and press K3, then select Structure and press K3. The Structure list opens with Markers OFF.

5. Select Markers and turn E3 once right. Markers reads ANCHORS and a Chord group row appears showing 1, then press K3. The footer reads APPLIED.

6. Press Play (grid (1,8)) and listen to two loops. The anchors C D E F sound as C C E E (MIDI 60, 60, 64, 64): D is equally near C and E and takes the lower one, and F is nearer E than G. The additions on steps 5 and 7 stay C. Press Stop.

7. Now the contrast. Select Markers and turn E3 once right. Markers reads EVERY 4, so only steps 1 and 5 are markers. Press K3.

8. Press Play. Step 1 and step 5 are C, which is already a chord tone, so nothing moves. D on step 2 and F on step 4 are not markers any more and return to their own pitches. The line plays MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65, 60 and 60 in each loop. Then press Stop.

Choosing Anchors snaps every anchor, and Every 4 snaps only the beats you choose. Deleting or disabling the group turns Markers OFF.

The captured version, [Captured Structure group and marker workflow](#structure/structure-anchor-chord-and-delete), covers steps 1 to 6 with Anchors and then deletes the group. Steps 7 and 8 are captured in [Mark every fourth step](#structure/structure-every-4-markers), which starts from the enabled C E G group with Foundation on and shows Markers set to Every 4 and the line playing 60, 62, 64, 65, 60, 60 in each loop.

features.title: Result and Reason

readme.excerpt:
Result shows each step's role (anchor, addition or fragment) and decision, and
Reason shows every reason an addition was left out, in order: `GAP`, then
`INTERLOCK CH02`; several reasons are named together (`GAP, INTERLOCK`). A
fragment step names its fragment and source, such as `FRAGMENT 1 P03` or
`KEPT ANCHOR`; a Structure marker step shows `MARKER CHORD G01` when its pitch
was snapped (or, before it plays, will be), `CHORD MISSING`, or the instruction
that kept its own pitch, such as `BYPASS NOTE MASK`, `BYPASS RANDOM`,
`BYPASS FIXED` or `BYPASS QUANTISED FIXED`. When a leader is set,
Result adds an Interlock row, and a queued change the loop boundary refused is
shown as `Rejected`. Reason is one screen of six rows: Step, Role with the
step's source patterns (`ADDITION P1,2`), Decision, Interlock, Velocity and
Pitch target. Its Interlock row is kept apart from the reasons: `ON` while
Interlock filters, `OFF` without a leader, or the bypass in force, such as
`RESYNC` or `PLAN LIMIT`, in which case gap and Amount still decide the step
as if Interlock were off.

Silence-aware interlock (Space: leaving room while another channel's notes are
still sounding) is not part of this release.

features.title: Harmony

readme.excerpt:
![Harmony Register settings in a vertical list on Norns](images/harmony-register.png)

![Harmony Pattern Tone Map on Norns](images/harmony-tone-map.png)

Harmony offers four mutually exclusive channel modes:

- Off follows the ordinary Mosaic pitch path exactly.
- Revoice takes the actual root and enabled chord-mask voices after Mosaic's
  pitch-class decisions, preserving their pitch classes and sounding count while
  choosing legal octaves and assignments.
- Pattern maps explicit effective relative values in the current merge binding
  to Bass, Inner1–3 or Top. Repeated mapped values reuse one pitch for the entire
  harmonic frame; unmapped values remain Raw. Random, fixed, absolute-mask and
  chord-mask events visibly bypass Pattern. Conflicting aliases fail closed.
- Ensemble assigns Bass/Inner/Top roles to one to five explicit monophonic
  channels. Each member retains its own rhythm, velocity, gate, clock and route,
  but its pitch is replaced by the shared frame. A conflicting local scale lock
  temporarily uses the ordinary pitch path (`LOCAL SCALE BYPASS`); a channel or
  step octave override does the same (`LOCAL OCTAVE BYPASS`).

Register rows set inclusive MIDI Low/High, Centre and Preferred leap for every
role. Smooth prioritises literal common tones and economical movement; Compact
prioritises register centre/spacing; Independent prioritises movement without a
common-tone score. Hard options cover crossing, exact unison, strict leap and
strict bass direction. Bass can be Root, an explicit Inversion tone, Smooth or
an exact Pedal. Revoice pedals must already be in its input material; only an
Ensemble group can explicitly allow a non-chord pedal.

The deterministic solver searches every legal pitch-class placement inside the
configured ranges (up to five voices) and never clamps an illegal result. A frame
with no solution silences affected mapped voices by default; Legacy fallback is
explicit. A bounded search reports `BUDGET EXCEEDED` rather than emitting a
partial answer. Preparing a frame does not change voice history: the first real
scheduled onset consumes it, while redraws, rests, failed probability, mute and
missing output do not. Delayed strums and arpeggios keep the pitch snapshot made
at their onset, and Note Off always releases the pitch and route actually sent.

![Harmony NO VOICING result on Norns](images/harmony-no-voicing.png)

The Channel grid remains the chronological trig/mask surface. Foundation anchors
and additions therefore appear as active steps there. After a step plays, the
Pattern Note grid moves that step's bright note LED to the final effective pitch
that the native 21-position note range can represent. Switch its upper, centred
or lower seven-note bank as usual to inspect octave placement. Raw and bypassed
events use the ordinary pre-Harmony position; turning Harmony Off restores the
ordinary merged/scale positions immediately. An exact pitch outside that native
range has no false in-range LED and remains available in Result/Note Dashboard.

This display is read-only: touching the projected Note fader still edits its
selected source-pattern value. Until the changed step plays again, the edited
source is displayed rather than a stale output. Final Harmony pitches are also
shown on Output (its Pitch and Sent rows) and on Harmony's Result screen, one row
per voice as the planned and sent note (`C3 > C3`). Result uses its Step row to
select one coherent event chain; on Note
Dashboard, holding a grid step temporarily inspects that step instead of combining
it with a later delayed event. A step with no recorded event says `NO EVENT` and
shows no planned or emitted pitch; it never borrows the latest event from another
step. This readout occupies the bottom two lines of the Note Dashboard, which is
the row tooltips use, so while a harmony event is being shown there the page
clears that row and tooltips are not visible on it. Result status names local scale/octave bypasses, explicit Legacy fallback
and the specific no-voicing reason. For an Ensemble group, any member bypass or failure is
surfaced even when another member has a valid voicing. The projection never writes
back into a shared pattern. Copy/save stores
versioned configuration, not running solver or phrase history. Missing optional
configuration loads as Off; unknown schema versions reject the project before it
replaces the active project.

details.title: Mode selection
details.text: Revoice places the actual root and enabled chord-mask voices in legal octaves. Pattern maps repeated effective relative values to roles. Ensemble assigns a shared harmonic frame to specified monophonic channels; each member retains its rhythm and route.

details.title: No voicing and fallback

A step with no event reads NO EVENT, which is different from a failed voicing. A solver budget failure does not emit a partial answer.

details.title: Note grid editing
details.text: After a played event, the Note grid displays the final pitch if it is within the native range. Editing a Note fader still edits the selected source pattern. Projected pitches are not written to that pattern.

details.title: Saving and loading
